description: Reduced semantic review cases from audited sourcing runs. These excerpts are test inputs, not sourcing evidence. These are manual/model-review cases, not an automated claim-truth gate. Evaluate with the current review instructions; compare decisions and reasoning, not exact wording.

cases.requirement: An equity funding round announced within 365 days; no requirement that the entire financing be equity
cases.source: The captured company announcement supports Glow's $180M venture funding on July 22, 2026. A captured secondary article identifies Series A. Only a truncated discovery search snippet says all-equity; neither captured funding page establishes that qualifier. The draft calls it an all-equity $180M Series A.
cases.reason: Keep the supported funding qualification and remove all-equity from the draft unless captured evidence establishes it. Missing support for an optional qualifier does not disqualify the company.

cases.requirement: Claims inflation named in company results within six months
cases.source: ERS published an April article discussing market-wide motor claims inflation. The article is commentary and contains no ERS financial results.
cases.reason: Company authorship does not make commentary company results.

cases.requirement: Underwriting or portfolio restructure, repositioning, exit or entry
cases.source: Arrow Global Insurance acquired a majority stake in Fusion Specialty. The announcement provides no change to its underwriting classes, appetite, portfolio or operating structure.
cases.reason: Ownership alone does not establish the requested business change.

cases.requirement: Rising combined ratio at the target company CNA Hardy
cases.source: CNA Hardy republishes CNA Financial group results. Group P&C combined ratio increased to 96.5% from 94.1%. No CNA Hardy-specific ratio is provided.
cases.reason: The parent metric is not attributed to the target subsidiary.

cases.requirement: Exclude insurers with a large consultancy already embedded
cases.source: The company biography describes a specialty insurer rather than a consulting firm. It gives no information about external operating-services relationships.
cases.reason: Being an insurer does not establish that no consultancy is embedded.

cases.requirement: Exclude insurers with a large consultancy already embedded
cases.source: A fresh company biography describes specialist underwriting. An earlier review cited a strategic multi-year consultancy engagement covering ongoing operating services; its current status has not been resolved.
cases.reason: Resolve the contrary relationship evidence before clearing the exclusion; neither discard it nor assume it lasts forever.

cases.requirement: Exclude insurers with a large consultancy currently embedded
cases.source: A 2022 release describes a completed seven-month finance implementation. A documented targeted current public screen found no evidence of an ongoing engagement, with private contracts unobservable.
cases.reason: The historical project alone does not prove a current exclusion. Preserve the current public-screen limitation.

cases.requirement: Underwriting or portfolio restructure, repositioning, exit or entry
cases.source: The company announced a new standalone Product Recall underwriting class with a dedicated team within the requested period.
cases.reason: The source establishes an actual qualifying class entry.

cases.requirement: 50–5,000 employees. Specialty carriers are judged on structure instead of premium size.
cases.source: The business is a specialty underwriting agency. Its verified published employee range is 2–10.
cases.reason: The premium-size exception does not waive the independent employee-size requirement.

cases.requirement: South African insurers, $50m upwards and 50+ employees. New Heads of Claims, Fraud, Underwriting or Compliance within 90 days. Any one listed signal suffices.
cases.source: The original request contains both size constraints. The saved interpretation includes only employee size and adds Operations to the appointment roles.
cases.reason: Preserve the independent financial threshold without inventing its metric, and restore the exact appointment roles. Do not approve the altered contract.

cases.requirement: Property, business-interruption or motor claims inflation in company results within six months.
cases.source: Santam reports catastrophe and large claims of R1.5bn versus R144m. Attritional claims are positive; the statement does not identify claims-cost inflation.
cases.reason: Higher loss totals do not establish a change in claims unit costs. Another supported listed signal could qualify under any-one logic.

cases.requirement: Claims inflation relevant to the selected South African insurance business within six months.
cases.source: OUTsurance reports lower premium inflation, increased natural-perils claims at Australian Youi, and more favourable weather and claims in South Africa.
cases.reason: Neither premium pricing nor Australian catastrophe totals establish the requested South African claims-cost inflation.

cases.requirement: Any one of company-published fraud figures within six months or an eligible leadership appointment within 90 days.
cases.source: The insurer’s current release quotes its CEO saying 4–6% of its annual claims are fraudulent. No leadership appointment is evidenced.
cases.reason: The fraud figures satisfy this stated alternative. Do not require the appointment as well; other independent company requirements still apply.
